tagline.text: Korean restaurants and grocers by Clark Airport

location.label: Location
location.text: Anunas, Cutcut and Pampang areas, Angeles City, Pampanga, along the Fil-Am Friendship Highway

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,500 (per person for a meal and shopping)

children.text: Korean restaurants, grocery stores, cafes and karaoke rooms line the Fil-Am Friendship Highway as it runs through Angeles City. It is close to Clark Airport, so it is handy for a first Korean meal on arrival day or for stocking up on Korean groceries.

Angeles Korean Town is not a separate tourist zone. It is the name given to the long strip of Korean businesses along the Fil-Am Friendship Highway as it passes through barangays such as Anunas, Cutcut and Pampang in Angeles City. Local media report that Korean businesses along this road have grown considerably, and with signs and neon lights in Hangul, a first visit feels a bit like walking through a busy street in Korea. Sources differ slightly on exactly where it starts and ends, so think of it roughly as the stretch running south from the Friendship Gate on the Clark Freeport side.

Clark explains why it grew here. Clark was once a US military base and is now home to Clark International Airport and the Freeport. Korean business owners and long-stay residents gathered in this area because it is close to the airport and living costs are low, and restaurants, grocery stores, hotels, spas and karaoke rooms followed. As a result it works as an everyday neighborhood for language students and resident Koreans as much as for visitors.

This is not a place you visit for sights. There are no ruins or viewpoints; the draw is samgyeopsal grilled at the table, Korean set meals, Korean-style fried chicken, jjajangmyeon, cafes and Korean grocery shopping. It is most useful for a meal on the day you arrive at or leave from Clark Airport, for a meal when Filipino food does not suit you, and for buying ramen, kimchi and sauces. Most Korean groceries can be found at the Korean marts along the road. They sell frozen meat and stew ingredients, rice cakes, honey ginger tea, ice cream and canned goods, enough for long-stay residents to shop here. Filipino restaurants and fast-food chains are mixed in along the same road, so you do not have to eat only Korean food.

There are also things to keep in mind. Angeles is known for its nightlife, and karaoke rooms and bars are mixed in with the restaurants here. This guide is written for daytime visits centered on restaurants and grocery stores, and it names only places that have operated for a long time or have been covered by the press. Hours and prices change often, so check before you go. Remember too that this street was not planned as a tourist attraction but formed naturally as private businesses gathered. There are no street information boards or an official visitor center, and information on shops relies heavily on Google Maps and Korean community reviews. Many shops open and close, so assume that details from articles or blogs may be out of date after a few years.

The signature dish of Korean Town is samgyeopsal, pork belly grilled at your table. It comes with kimchi, pickled radish and lettuce for wrapping, and set meals such as bibimbap and bulgogi are common too. A pork galbi restaurant in Cutcut has been reported as open 24 hours. When you order meat, side dishes usually come along with lettuce, garlic and ssamjang. For larger groups, set menus are often more economical.

blocks.title: Korean fried chicken and snack food

children.text: There are specialty shops for Korean-style fried chicken in several flavors, such as seasoned, soy and garlic, and places that serve tteokbokki and jjajangmyeon. Some chicken shops serve side dishes when you eat in.

Korean marts along the road sell frozen meat, stew ingredients, ramen, snacks, rice cakes and seasonings. Some have been reported as open 24 hours, which is convenient for late-night or early-morning shopping.

A cafe and restaurant on the upper floors of a building on the Friendship Highway has been featured for its roof deck seating and small library. It serves all-day breakfast and desserts, which makes it a good place to rest. This cafe, which occupies the 4th to 6th floors, was reported in a 2022 article as open daily from 10 a.m. to midnight, so confirm its hours before you go.

Hangul signs and neon lights run one after another and create a scene resembling a Korean shopping district. Many people take photos, but the road is wide and busy, so walking conditions are not good.
You can combine a visit with Clark Freeport's golf courses, malls and parks on the same day. The most natural plan is to eat in Korean Town and then head up toward Clark.

Even the same samgyeopsal differs from shop to shop in seasoning and thickness of the meat. There are also Chinese-style Korean dishes such as jjajangmyeon and jjamppong, plus sundubu and stews, so it is fun to compare one or two places a day. Some places keep the spice mild for Filipino tastes, so ask about the spice level when you order.
Take Grab or a taxi from Clark Airport or your Angeles hotel to the Anunas section of the Friendship Highway. Check the opening hours of the restaurant you plan to visit before you arrive.

Have samgyeopsal or a Korean set meal for lunch. Grilling meat at lunch leaves the smell on your clothes, so it helps to bring a change of clothes. Some places take orders for two portions or more rather than one, so tell them your party size first.
Buy ramen, kimchi, sauces and snacks at a Korean mart, then rest with coffee at a nearby cafe. Marts reported as open 24 hours can be used late at night, but this may change, so confirm.
Take Korean fried chicken or snack food back to your hotel, or head up toward Clark Freeport for the next part of your day.
The road is long, so walking between shops is far. It is easier to eat and shop in one area and use Grab or a tricycle to move.

items.title: Airport link route
items.subtitle: First meal on the day you land at Clark

children.text: After landing at Clark International Airport, take Grab or a taxi to Korean Town for your first meal. It is fairly close to the airport, but the exact time depends on traffic.
Buy water and snacks at a mart before you go to your hotel.

From Pasay or Cubao in Manila, take a Pampanga-bound bus such as Victory Liner and get off at Angeles or the Dau Terminal in Mabalacat. The trip is quoted at about 2–4 hours depending on traffic, and fares are quoted in a range of about ₱160~300.
From the Dau Terminal to central Angeles, a taxi or jeepney reportedly takes about 15–20 minutes. Check the operator for the latest schedule and fares.
By car from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA), the drive is quoted at about 1 hour 15 minutes in good traffic and the cost at about ₱700~1,100. A pre-booked airport car is the safer choice.
Exact times and fares vary widely with the time of day and traffic.

The Friendship Highway stretch is close to Clark International Airport (CRK), so take Grab or a taxi. Asiana Airlines and low-cost carriers have been reported to serve Clark, but routes change often, so check the latest information.
Jeepneys and tricycles run along the road, and Grab is available. The shops are far apart, so decide on your transport in advance.
Since it centers on indoor restaurants and marts, the season matters little. In the rainy season, however, heavy rain can cause traffic jams or flooding on the road.
If you want to walk around in the daytime, the morning or late afternoon in the dry season is better.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Avoid walking at midday and stay mostly indoors.
Using Grab and leaving extra time in your plans is recommended.

For lodging you can consider hotels and guesthouses within Korean Town, hotels in Clark Freeport, or hotels in central Angeles. If your goal is meals and shopping, staying closer to Clark Airport reduces travel. Central Angeles (the Balibago side) has a strong nightlife atmosphere, so family travelers should check the location of their lodging in advance.

Food divides into samgyeopsal restaurants, 24-hour restaurants serving pork galbi and jjajangmyeon, Korean fried chicken shops, rooftop cafes and Korean marts. Places that have been featured in the press include a pork galbi restaurant in Cutcut, a Korean barbecue house in Pampang, and a chicken shop and a cafe along the Friendship Highway, but closures and moves are frequent, so check on Google Maps whether a place is currently open.

Restaurant prices often feel cheap compared with Korea, but meat dishes add up quickly as the party grows. Check your order and whether service charge is included before you pay. For the featured cafe restaurant, Western dishes were quoted in 2022 at pizza from ₱330, pasta from ₱180, rice meals from ₱160 and drinks from ₱140.
Samgyeopsal places are usually busy in the evening, when demand is high. You will wait less at lunch or early evening.
Some marts and restaurants have been reported as open 24 hours, but this may change. Check first if you plan to go late.
The shops are far apart and hard to walk between. Install the Grab app in advance.
More places accept cards, but small marts and street stalls may need cash, so bring small bills.
The smell of grilled meat sticks to your clothes, so check whether your hotel can do laundry or bring a change of clothes.
Korean is understood at many places, but some have Filipino staff, so pointing to menu photos makes ordering easy.
Some shops offer delivery. Minimum order amounts differ by shop.
Put frozen and chilled food bought at a mart into your hotel fridge right away on hot days.
Reading local Korean community cafe posts together with Google Maps reviews makes it easier to filter out shops that are still open. Favor reviews posted within the last few months.

Violent crime against Koreans has been reported in the Korean Town area, including a Korean national shot dead in a robbery near a bank on Friendship Highway at about 1:50 p.m. on April 20, 2025. Avoid moving alone at night and avoid showing valuables.
At night, do not wander alone into quiet alleys; call a Grab instead.
Traffic moves fast on the road. Cross at signals or footbridges.
At entertainment venues such as karaoke rooms and bars, overcharging and touting can occur. Ask the price first and get a receipt.
Do not exchange money or make small deals on the street. Use an official exchange counter or a mart.
Security and regulations change often, so check your government's travel advisory before departure, for example the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and embassy notices for Korean travelers.
Beyond the Friendship Gate lies Clark Freeport. With golf courses, parks and malls, it can be combined on the same day.
This is the central city of Pampanga, known for its Christmas lanterns and Filipino cuisine. Count on roughly
40 minutes–1 hour
by car.
A dormant volcano rising above the Pampanga plain, known as a day-hike destination. Check the entry rules locally.
